preamble: Debuccalization of a rhotic to the glottal stop [ʔ]. In Egyptian, /r/ (together with /t/ and /j/) became /ʔ/ at the end of a stressed syllable and was eventually lost word-finally. Wiktionary's reconstructions, following Loprieno, show Old Egyptian ħaɾ 'upon' and çuɾ 'under' as later ħaʔ and çuʔ, and Egyptian ḥr 'face' as Classical Coptic /hoʔ/. No other regular one-step r > ʔ change has been confirmed; the Kuki-Chin cases go through an intermediate velar stop and belong in r_to_k and k_to_glottal_stop.

examples.note: The coda r of the stressed syllable became a glottal stop, which Classical Coptic reconstructions keep as /ʔ/.
The r survives before suffix pronouns, as in Sahidic ϩⲁⲣⲟ⸗.

examples.to: later Egyptian /çuʔ/, Sahidic ϩⲁ-, Bohairic ϧⲁ-
examples.note: Pronominal forms such as Bohairic ϧⲁⲣⲟ⸗ keep the r.
